races.name: JenningsBet In Newcastle Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

runners_data.name: Inspiring Speeches
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a recent win over 12f on Good ground (1/12f/GOO); steps back from 14f trips and jockey Mr Aiden Blakemore (3lb claimer) is a positive, but the OR 50 mark and inconsistent form string limit expectations even if the trip suits.

runners_data.name: Ivynator
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran who races off the pace by instinct; OR 48 at the bottom of the weights is tempting but a recent string of double-figure finishes and no win over this course and distance in recent form make it hard to trust.

runners_data.name: The Pug
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up type that races from deep; Tim Easterby runner Mr Josh Murphy in the saddle, but the form string of 474903 reflects inconsistency, and the horse's two AW runs at this trip resulted in finishes of 9th — hard to get excited at OR 46.

runners_data.name: Yurinov
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's six-year-old wants to race from the back but will find itself shuffled into mid-division in this shape; has placed on AW at 12f and 14f before, yet a string of 5th-7th finishes signals a horse that runs creditably without threatening.

runners_data.name: Beat The Odds
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain four-year-old who instinctively drops to the rear of the field; a 46-day absence is a flag, and the form figures on AW standard-type surfaces show no wins or places — hard to fancy stepping into a 14-runner amateur riders' handicap.

runners_data.name: He's Our Cracker
runners_data.note: Top-rated hold-up horse at OR 58 with a recent win over 10f on AW Standard; wears a tongue-strap and cheekpieces, jockey Mr Freddie Robson (5lb claimer) gives 5lb back, and a genuine course record means the horse is competitive — naturally races from deep, which this shape may compromise.

runners_data.name: Maple
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner and race-shaper; Ruth Jefferson's five-year-old has placed twice at 10f on AW Standard and gets her own way from the gate — the Standard to Slow surface and a 27-day break are manageable risks, and she will dictate terms throughout.

runners_data.name: Wicklow Way
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's four-year-old has a win over 10f on Standard AW (1/10f/STA) and placed over 8f on Good — naturally prefers to race from the back, but this course form is real; jockey Mr Felix Foster (7lb claimer) is a significant weight relief given the 148lb burden.

runners_data.name: Langton Wold
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's seven-year-old returns from a 640-day absence (556 days for this jockey combination) which is an enormous red flag — the horse has form at staying distances on Good and Soft ground, and the prominence style means he could track Maple, but the layoff makes him deeply unreliable.

runners_data.name: Luan
runners_data.note: James Ferguson's four-year-old has a warning flag for fading in the finish, which is damaging in a slowly-run race likely to demand a genuine late effort; four AW Standard runs recently all resulted in finishes of 5th or worse, and the hold-up style is fully genuine but undermined by the fading tendency.

runners_data.name: The Ubermensch
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's top-rated runner at OR 60 with the highest ceiling in the race; a consistent placer over 10f-12f on AW Standard and Good, wears a tongue-strap and cheekpieces, and jockey Mr Jack Lander (5lb claimer) adds value — the hold-up style suits a slowly-run race less well than a true test, but the class edge is real.

runners_data.name: Kitsune Power
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby runner at OR 59 with a strong recent record over 12f and 14f on Good ground — four of the last five runs have been 2nd, 3rd, 3rd or 4th, suggesting a genuine each-way profile; the 8-day turnaround and tongue-strap are fine, and 12f trips suit, though all the AW Standard form shows no wins.

runners_data.name: Glitter Code
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's four-year-old wears a visor and has form placing at 8f and 10f on Good; the 155lb weight and 28-day break are manageable, but a history of wide-draw finishes of 10th and 9th on AW Standard is a concern — needs to improve markedly on that surface.

runners_data.name: Royal Blaze
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans' five-year-old has an AW win (1/12f/STA) and placed twice on 12f Soft and Standard, plus wears a tongue-strap and cheekpieces; the 9-day turnaround is fine and the horse has handled 9f-12f trips, making the stamina question less concerning — naturally races from deep but has the form profile to be competitive if the shape suits.

races.paceDynamic: Maple is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a 14-runner field at 1m2f on a Standard to Slow surface, she is set to control this race at a measured, uncontested gallop from the front. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types — Ivynator, The Pug, Yurinov, Beat The Odds, He's Our Cracker, Wicklow Way, Luan, The Ubermensch, Kitsune Power, Glitter Code, and Royal Blaze all prefer to race off the pace — meaning Maple faces no serious early pressure and can dictate a tempo entirely on her own terms. Langton Wold and Inspiring Speeches are the only other prominent-profile runners who might press forward and give Maple some company, but neither is a natural front-runner and neither is likely to drastically quicken the pace. This race shape strongly favours a hold-up profile that can travel smoothly through the pack and deliver a sustained late run, as Maple's uncontested lead at a modest gallop over a distance of ground on a slow surface will set up a proper stamina test rather than a burn-up — horses with the class to cruise through a slowly-run race and finish strongly are best placed to exploit the scenario.

scenarios.body: If the tempo is slow enough that Maple steals a meaningful break and her rivals leave it too late to reel her in.

scenarios.body: If the race develops into a bunched affair through the middle stages and a horse with superior form or rating cuts through from mid-division.

scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Swamp Leader Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and Maple weakens sharply in the closing stages, triggering a mass late charge from the rear.
scenarios.body: If the pace is faster than expected and Maple weakens sharply in the closing stages, triggering a mass late charge from the rear.

watchPoints.text: Maple's uncontested lead is the pivotal factor in this race — if she jumps quickly and is allowed a soft lead by Mr Freddie Robson and the rest, the entire field could be chasing a phantom for too long.

Langton Wold's 640-day absence is a serious risk factor — if he shows signs of rustiness in the early stages and drifts wide, he could cause traffic issues for the midfield hold-up pack travelling on his outside.

With at least nine genuine hold-up types all converging on the same space from the 4f pole onwards, Kitsune Power, The Ubermensch, and He's Our Cracker are all at risk of losing momentum if the inside rail becomes congested on the home turn.

Luan's flagged tendency to fade in the finish is worth monitoring — if he travels well into contention before weakening, he could act as a moving obstruction for those finishing strongest, particularly Royal Blaze and Glitter Code who may need room at the same moment.

The going is confirmed Standard to Slow rather than Standard, which adds a stamina premium over 1m2f — horses with proven AW staying form such as He's Our Cracker and Royal Blaze carry an edge over those whose best form has come on quicker ground.

races.name: JenningsBet In Shiremoor Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
JenningsBet In Pelton Handicap

runners_data.name: Bowood
runners_data.note: Won last time over 8f on Standard and has five places from seven runs on similar going; hold-up style means she needs a race that falls apart late, but trainer Furtado has two runners today and she arrives fresh at 21 days — a sneaky each-way threat if the pace is strong enough to create a gap.|

runners_data.name: Montezin
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a win and three places from six runs on Standard-type going; drops back in trip from his recent Goodwood run and Cam Hardie rode him last time — the headgear (tp) suggests connections are trying to keep him focused and he should get a handy position without fighting for it.|

runners_data.name: Intrusively
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with zero wins or places from his two runs on Standard going (2/15 sim-going record), no victories in 15 career runs; the visor is on but his record on this surface and style mismatch make him hard to recommend.|

runners_data.name: They All Know Me
runners_data.note: Strong recent form — second and eighth in competitive 7f handicaps — but his natural hold-up style cannot be accommodated in a field this deep in rear-runners; he will race further forward than ideal, which may not be a problem given he has won from a prominent position before, but his best form requires space he may not find.|

runners_data.name: Stanage
runners_data.note: Off 89 days, which is the longest break in the field, and his hood (h) suggests a tendency to idle; races from hold-up style naturally but will be pushed into midfield by the crowded rear — his form on Standard and Soft going is limited and the layoff is a real concern.|

runners_data.name: Jazzy Baby
runners_data.note: Consistent placer with four places from eight starts on Standard ground and a win over this course and distance last year; prominent style suits the projected race shape well and Josephine Gordon is an astute jockey for this type of race — her recent form string shows she goes well fresh.|

runners_data.name: Kanishka
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a win and two places from three runs on Standard-type going; the headgear (p) has been consistent and Brian Ellison's yard (T14: 0/25) is quiet but Luke Morris rides with good course knowledge — his profile over a mile on this surface is genuinely strong.|

runners_data.name: Victory Ace
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard last time and followed with a second; John Butler's yard (T14: 2/19) is in light form overall but Victory Ace himself is on a roll, and his prominent style means he should get a clean run just behind the pace — the step to a mile is the only question mark.|

runners_data.name: Asian Journey
runners_data.note: Two wins and consistent placing across recent starts for Sam England; the headgear (t) is consistent and his sim-going record of 10 places from 15 is deceptive — he is a natural hold-up horse pushed forward by field congestion, so his best finishing effort may be curtailed by having nowhere to settle.|

runners_data.name: Chuzzlewit
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's gelding has four places from nine Standard-ground runs but no wins on the surface; his natural rear-running style is compromised here — he'll race in midfield without being able to generate his characteristic late momentum, making his chance structural rather than personal.|

runners_data.name: Callianassa
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner and pace-setter; carries OR 80 and the highest weight in the field at 142lbs, and the [STYLE_FIT] flag notes she may not fully reproduce her best, but no rival will seriously contest her lead — her fate depends entirely on whether the Standard to Slow ground allows her to maintain her tempo through the final two furlongs.|

runners_data.name: Harry The Rogue
runners_data.note: Has two places from three runs on Standard ground over 8f and a placed effort last time; prominent style gives him an ideal positional draw against this race shape, and Jason Hart is an excellent judge of pace — the 10-runner finishing position over 10f on Good last time suggests the step back to a mile and easier going suits.|

runners_data.name: Sailthisshipalone
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with headgear (tp) and a very poor sim-going record of zero wins or places from 15 Standard-ground runs; won over 8f on Soft last time but this surface profile is genuinely alarming and Tom Eaves will need something very different from the track today.|

runners_data.name: Racingbreaks Ryder
runners_data.note: Charles Hills runner who has not won on Standard going in five attempts and has been beaten a combined 48+ lengths in his last three; his one place at Standard came over 8f at a different track — the form makes him very hard to include at any meaningful probability despite the competent jockey booking.|

races.paceDynamic: Callianassa is the one confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner field and, with no identified rival likely to seriously contest the early lead, she should be able to dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable tempo on Standard to Slow ground over a mile at Newcastle. With Montezin, Kanishka, Victory Ace, Harry The Rogue, and Jazzy Baby all prominent-style runners also in the mix, the early sections of the race will see a cluster racing forwardly, but none of them are likely to fight Callianassa for the actual lead — they will simply ensure the gallop is honest rather than a crawl. That honest-but-not-suicidal tempo over a mile, combined with Standard to Slow going, typically compresses the field and limits the advantage available to true hold-up horses, favouring runners who track the pace closely and can sustain their effort into the home straight. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the positional map can accommodate — They All Know Me, Stanage, Asian Journey, and Chuzzlewit are all natural rear-runners who will be unable to secure their preferred deep position and must race further forward than ideal, reducing the likelihood of a late sweeping finish. **Tactical verdict: horses racing in a prominent-to-midfield position — close enough to the pace to exploit any late drift from Callianassa — hold the structural advantage in this race shape.**

watchPoints.text: Callianassa (Conor Whiteley, 5lb claimer) sets the sole early pace — if the claimer misjudges the tempo and goes too fast for Standard to Slow ground, she will dramatically compress the finish and hand the race to the prominent trackers behind her.

They All Know Me (David Nolan) and Chuzzlewit (Shay Farmer) are natural hold-up horses who cannot get to the rear in this 14-runner field — watch whether they settle in midfield or fight for position early, as restless travel will cost them their late kick.

Victory Ace (Ray Dawson) is on a three-run roll with a win and a second — if he travels smoothly just behind Callianassa in fourth or fifth, he is the most dangerous prominent type to accelerate past a tiring leader in the straight.

Stanage (Joanna Mason) has not run for 89 days — the longest layoff in the field — and the hood is not a confidence signal; watch in the pre-parade for any signs of freshness or reluctance that might telegraph a below-par effort.

Sailthisshipalone (Tom Eaves) and Racingbreaks Ryder (Callum Rodriguez) have between them zero places from their last 30 combined Standard-going runs — if either markets unexpectedly short, that is a strong signal of significant stable/market information to monitor.

races.name: JenningsBet In Delves Hoppings Fillies' Stakes (Fillies' And Mares' Group 3)

runners_data.name: Dreamasar
runners_data.note: Top-form filly with back-to-back wins including over this course and distance on Standard; P McDonald is a powerful booking, and at 1m2f she looks suited — the step back to a Group race after handicap wins is the key question.|

runners_data.name: Uluru
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's 5yo is a genuine hold-up type and represents the stable alongside Ashariba; recent form has been moderate (three 6ths) and she hasn't won since a 1m2f success on good ground, so needs rivals to soften the pace for her.|

runners_data.name: Botagoz
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's 3yo has a fine record of 1-1-3 and clearly holds ability, but her natural instinct is to race prominently — here, with the prominent slots already occupied by bigger, older fillies, she is likely to find herself shuffled back into a role that doesn't suit her best.|

runners_data.name: Ashariba
runners_data.note: Menuisier's other runner won twice on soft ground and has decent prominent-style form, though her best effort here came on softer going than Standard To Slow; she too is a racer who prefers to be on the speed but will be crowded back into midfield by the race shape.|

runners_data.name: Diamond Rain
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter and market leader at OR 114 for Charlie Appleby; her course-and-distance win on Standard going is directly relevant, and Buick's front-running read from the front will be hard to unpick — the STYLE_FIT flag reflects the competitive nature of the field rather than a stylistic mismatch.|

runners_data.name: Sky Safari
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back at this track over this trip on Standard going, and her proximity record in similar conditions is strong — she wears a tongue-tie and is the natural second horse to Diamond Rain in the early order, making her a natural each-way beneficiary of the pace scenario.|

runners_data.name: Alla Stella
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's 4yo has placed twice over 1m2f on good ground but her recent form line reads 6-3-9 and she has not yet won beyond 9f; a genuine prominent racer, she will not get the lead in this shape and must demonstrate she can be effective when racing behind horses.|

races.paceDynamic: Diamond Rain is the confirmed front-runner here and, with William Buick in the saddle, she is likely to control this from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop on the Newcastle AW surface. Sky Safari and Dreamasar are genuine prominent types who will press for position behind her, creating a compact, organised early order rather than a burning pace. This field carries more prominent horses than the race shape can accommodate — Ashariba, Botagoz, and Alla Stella are all natural prominent racers who will be squeezed back into a midfield role they do not naturally favour. The result is a race likely run at a controlled, honest tempo that rewards the horse who can travel close to the pace and quicken from a good position — making the prominent profile, and specifically those who genuinely secure it, the dominant beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Diamond Rain's early pace is the fulcrum of the race — watch whether Buick eases her into a slow or medium gallop, as an uncontested amble could turn the final two furlongs into a sprint that compromises her and benefits Sky Safari or Dreamasar.

The redistribution of Botagoz, Ashariba, and Alla Stella into midfield is a live threat to their chances — watch the first two furlongs for traffic, checked positions, or wide manoeuvres as these natural front-runners scramble for ground.

Uluru's hold-up profile is genuine but she has finished 6th three times recently — watch whether she gets any cover in midfield on the back straight, as an exposed wide position at Newcastle's long straight could drain her before the finish.

Sky Safari's tongue-tie is worth noting — she has won twice at this course and trip, and her rider Muscutt knows the track well; if she tracks Diamond Rain smoothly through the first half, she could prove the hardest to hold off late.

Dreamasar carries 133lbs as a 4yo stepping up from handicap company to Group 3 — watch whether she travels within herself in the prominent position or gets into a pulling battle early with the fillies ahead of her.

runners_data.name: Seven Questions
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer for Robert Cowell who has shown she can finish from off the pace; her best recent effort was a win at 5f on Good ground but she has form on softer surfaces, and the Standard to Slow going here is no concern — her task is whether enough pace is generated to suit her from the rear.

runners_data.name: Fidelius
runners_data.note: Cowell's in-form sprinter arrives on the back of a win and a second, both at 5f on Standard ground, which is the most directly relevant form in the field; a natural front-end racer, he will likely find himself racing further back than ideal given the traffic ahead of him, which tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: Vantheman
runners_data.note: Suited by a strongly-run 5f on good or faster ground based on his strike-rate, but his two course-and-distance efforts in similar going have been modest; a genuine forward-going type who will struggle to express that style fully with Gaeli and others ahead of him.

runners_data.name: Canon's House
runners_data.note: Easterby's runner has a placed effort on softer ground and is a true hold-up horse who will sit deep; his recent form suggests he can find the frame in competitive 5f sprints, though his finishing kick on a flat track without a strong pace to chase into looks his limiting factor.

runners_data.name: Paddy's Day
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue tie and has placed form on Standard and Standard to Slow ground; the six-year-old is by nature a horse that wants to be close to the pace, but with so many rivals competing for that position he may end up further back than his best form requires, softening his win chance.

runners_data.name: Al Shabab Storm
runners_data.note: Carries top weight on a mark of 98 and is ridden by the claiming apprentice Conor Whiteley; his recent turf form has been poor — four out-of-the-frame efforts — and his best runs came at 6f and further on Standard ground, making this shorter trip on current form a concern.

runners_data.name: Gaeli
runners_data.note: Marco Ghiani takes the ride for Marco Botti on the confirmed front runner; she won over this course and distance on Standard ground and is wearing a hood, and with no confirmed rival to press her she should get a soft lead — her STYLE_FIT flag reflects that her hold on the prominent slot is the key variable.

runners_data.name: Purosangue
runners_data.note: Cowell has three runners in this race and Purosangue is his hold-up type; he has finished fourth on four of his last five starts but none on this course or going, and with zero wins from 15 runs on similar ground his record in this scenario offers little encouragement despite a tidy profile.

runners_data.name: Kylian
runners_data.note: Hood-wearing Cowell runner on a mark of 95 who has winning form over 6f on Good and Soft; he has been freshened up after a run 20 days ago and is a prominent racer who should get a slot just behind Gaeli — his class and course experience make him a logical challenger if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Another Baar
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and ran just eight days ago, making this a quick turnaround; his only recent win came at 5f on Good ground and his last five runs on similar surfaces have not produced a finish, suggesting confidence in his current form is limited despite the yard's two-from-fifteen recent strike rate.

runners_data.name: Corolla Point
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's four-year-old has won twice at 5f, both on softer and Good ground, and arrives after a 43-day break; his last three turf runs have produced two placed efforts at this distance and he is a legitimate prominent racer without the redistribution problem, giving him a cleaner profile than several rivals.

runners_data.name: The Man
runners_data.note: Off for 112 days — the longest layoff in the field — and has struggled for form since his placed effort, with three consecutive sixth-place finishes; Richard Spencer's charge has placed form at 5f on Standard ground but the lengthy absence at this level of competition is a significant flag.

runners_data.name: Sir Yoshi
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse from Geoffrey Harker's yard whose recent 6f form has been poor — two very wide runs — but who showed a 5f profile previously with two second-placed efforts; the drop back to the minimum trip could help, but his record on similar ground reads two from fifteen with no wins.

runners_data.name: Air Force One
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald rides the five-year-old who won at 5f on Soft ground earlier in his career and has shown consistent place form; wears a visor, has run twice on Standard to Slow ground without a win, and while he is a natural front-end type his limited recent returns in this company make him better placed as a frame contender.

races.paceDynamic: Gaeli is the confirmed front runner and, with no direct rival willing to press from the outset, should secure an uncontested lead through the early stages of this 5f contest on Standard to Slow ground at Newcastle. The redistribution flags tell a significant story: Fidelius, Vantheman, Paddy's Day, Corolla Point, Kylian, Another Baar and Air Force One are all natural prominent racers, yet the map cannot accommodate them all in that position — Gaeli holds the cleaner berth, with Kylian and Corolla Point most likely to lock in just behind on class and recent form. With one front runner dictating at a measured, uncontested clip on a flat track, the pace is unlikely to be genuinely searching, which historically at Newcastle 5f compresses the finish and benefits horses travelling smoothly in the first two to three off the leader rather than pure closers making up big ground. This race shape strongly favours the handy, prominent-to-midfield profile that can track Gaeli without covering extra ground, as true hold-up types will be left with too little time to close on a comfortable early tempo.

watchPoints.text: Watch Gaeli's behaviour in the early stalls and at the break — if she misses the kick or is slowly away, the entire pace map resets and a contested early gallop becomes likely, opening the race up significantly for hold-up horses Seven Questions and Purosangue.

The cluster of redistributed prominent types — Fidelius, Vantheman, Kylian, Corolla Point and Paddy's Day — will jostle for position in the first furlong; any bumping or checking in that group could cause interference and compromise several of the most fancied runners simultaneously.

Al Shabab Storm's poor recent turf form combined with top weight and a claiming rider is a potential market drifter to monitor; if his SP drifts markedly in the ring it may confirm that connections have no strong expectation on current form.

The Man's 112-day absence is the standout fitness flag in the field — watch his pre-race appearance and whether he is noticeably fit or shows signs of needing the run, as a first outing after a long break in a competitive 14-runner sprint handicap is a tough ask.

Standard to Slow ground is marginally slower than the Standard the going report is listed as in the race header — the actual going report confirms Standard to Slow for this race, which will bias the outcome slightly toward class horses and those with proven form on give in the ground rather than pure speed types.

runners_data.note: Prominent-style 4yo for Nigel Tinkler with a 3lb claimer; course form is modest (sim-going 2/15 over just two comparable runs) and recent efforts at Goodwood suggest a step up in consistency is needed, though the return to AW standard ground is a mild positive.

runners_data.name: Little Mi Mi
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with strong form on Standard/AW going (9/15 sim-going, 2 wins 6 places) and has won twice at 5f on this surface; Iain Jardine is in decent 14-day form (4/20) and Andrew Mullen knows this horse well — one of the standout pace profiles in the race.

runners_data.name: Maldevious
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison 4yo fitted with hood; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural instinct is to race from the rear, pushed into a midfield map position here because the field is overloaded with closers — his best form is at 6f rather than 5f and that trip drop is a concern on top of the positional compromise.

runners_data.name: Miss Rainbow
runners_data.note: Prominent 5yo for Tracy Waggott fitted with visor; has won at 5f on Good and placed at 6f, with a recent win giving confidence, though her sim-going record is just 3/15 and the Standard to Slow surface is one she has not excelled on historically.

runners_data.name: Henery Hawk
runners_data.note: Prominent veteran with outstanding sim-going credentials (14/15 comparable runs, 3 wins 9 places on Standard/AW) who shaped well last time; Luke Morris keeps the ride and the 5f trip is ideal — this profile arguably suits the likely race shape as well as any horse in the field.

runners_data.name: Irish Nectar
runners_data.note: Hold-up 5yo fitted with blinkers; best form has come at 6f on Standard AW (2nd in sim-going) and the drop to 5f is a genuine stamina-in-reverse concern — Connor Planas takes the mount for Michael Herrington who has had 3 winners in 14 days, but closing from the rear in a 5f sprint is a tough ask here.

runners_data.name: Sports Coach
runners_data.note: Hold-up 5yo for Antony Brittain; best recent turf form is at 5f but sim-going record is patchy (5/15, 1W 2P) and he has struggled to reproduce handicap form when off the pace over the minimum trip — the positional demands of this race shape do not play to his strengths.

runners_data.name: Call To Action
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner fitted with blinkers for Michael and David Easterby; STYLE_FIT flag notes he will be racing in a slightly forced role here relative to his wider career profile, and while he will set the pace his ability to sustain it on Standard to Slow ground at this OR of 75 is the key question — sim-going is only 2/11.

runners_data.name: Ancient State
runners_data.note: Prominent 4yo for Adam Kirby (trainer) with strong AW form (10/13 sim-going, 3W 6P); has won twice at 5f on Standard and been placed twice more, comes into this just 7 days after a run, and the headgear (ear-tabs) is consistent — one of the most streetwise profiles in the race at this distance and surface.

runners_data.name: Tiriac
runners_data.note: Hold-up 6yo for Paul Midgley; won at 5f on Standard AW last time out (1/5f/STA) after a string of disappointing efforts, and the bounce factor after a 34-day break is worth noting — David Nolan takes the mount but a natural closer needs luck from off the pace in a 14-runner sprint.

runners_data.name: Blind Beggar
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran fitted with blinkers; sim-going record is poor (1/15) and recent form reads 0006 at 6f, suggesting the horse is out of sorts — even if positional factors aligned, the form base does not support confidence at this trip or going.

runners_data.name: Tanjen
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Tim Easterby (6 winners from 89 runs in 14 days, indicating stable form); pushed into a midfield map position because the field is saturated with closers — his best AW form is at 5f on Standard and he has won twice in similar conditions, but the positional compromise is a real obstacle in a fast-filling 5f sprint.

runners_data.name: Fierce
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley hold-up 6yo; has placed three times at 5f on Standard AW (7/15 sim-going) and the form string shows consistent placing without winning — a true back-of-field horse mapped forward due to redistribution, Jason Hart will try to get a position closer than natural but the style compromise dampens the win chance meaningfully.

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Hold-up 7yo for Tristan Davidson; won at 5f on Good recently but the AW sim-going record (8/15) includes an 8th on Standard and form has been patchy — Rowan Scott takes the ride, and like the other redistributed closers in this race, the inability to drop to the rail and make a clean late run is a structural disadvantage in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Call To Action is the lone confirmed front-runner and will stride into an uncontested lead from the gates, setting a sustainable tempo over the 5f on a Standard to Slow surface — conditions that will keep the fractions honest rather than burn-and-bust. Ancient State and Little Mi Mi are the most likely to press Call To Action from prominent positions, giving the race a clean shape with a small lead group and a genuine gallop rather than a crawl. The Standard to Slow going at Newcastle AW rewards horses who can track efficiently and quicken off a genuine pace rather than those forced to make up excessive ground from the back. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and pounce in the final furlong, as the single front-runner is unlikely to be pressured into a suicidal pace but will also not be gifted an easy lone lead. The field holds more hold-up types than can genuinely be accommodated at the rear — Tanjen, Fierce, Harb and Maldevious are true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map, and of those Fierce and Tanjen are most likely to at least secure a stalking position given their recent form profile, though none can guarantee their natural position in this congested 14-runner sprint.

watchPoints.text: Ancient State has the strongest AW 5f form profile in the field (10/13 sim-going, 3W 6P) and races for trainer Adam Kirby just 7 days after a run — watch for him to press Call To Action from a prominent position and take over late.

Henery Hawk's sim-going record is exceptional (14/15 comparable runs) and is one of the most unexposed profiles over 5f Standard AW in this field — Luke Morris will look to sit just off the pace and his course record suggests he converts regularly in this scenario.

Call To Action has a STYLE_FIT flag and while he will lead, his ability to sustain it on Standard to Slow over 5f at OR 75 is uncertain — if he weakens inside the final furlong, he could cause interference to horses tracking him closely.

The four redistributed hold-up horses (Tanjen, Fierce, Harb, Maldevious) will all be seeking a position closer than natural at the break in a 14-runner field — watch for crowding and bumping in the opening furlong as these horses are forced forward out of their instinctive pattern.

Little Mi Mi has the best proven Standard/AW going record among the prominent types (9/15 sim-going, 2W 6P) and Andrew Mullen is a strong jockey at Newcastle AW — if she gets a clean passage from a prominent position she is very much in the finish.

runners_data.name: Newyorkstateofmind
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old hold-up specialist for Ruth Carr and Joanna Mason, with similar-going form showing eight runs without a win on comparable surfaces; true back-marker type whose position on the map understates how far back she will be, making her dependent on a strong pace she is unlikely to get here.

runners_data.name: Summer Rain
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's four-year-old has finished fourth on this course and surface and carries hold-up habits into a race where the pace is expected to be modest; Sam James takes the ride but the soft tempo will make it hard to generate the closing momentum this horse needs.

runners_data.name: She's A Goldigger
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald partners this Mark Walford-trained mare who carries a headgear flag and has a modest similar-going record of no wins and no places from two qualifying runs; her hold-up style is a liability in a small-pace scenario and she drops into the race on 15 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Invincible Annice
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott sends out this four-year-old wearing a visor with a flagged tendency to fade in the finish, and her similar-going record of one win from thirteen runs on comparable surfaces does not inspire confidence; she arrives 41 days fresh and is mapped to midfield despite being a genuine rear-of-the-field type.

runners_data.name: Sally Anne's Dream
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's runner has been off 213 days — the longest layoff in the field — and carries a fade-in-finish flag alongside a blank similar-going record; this lengthy absence, combined with a true hold-up style squeezed into a redistributed midfield position, makes her an obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Miners Gamble
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's five-year-old steps down sharply from ten-furlong trips to six furlongs here, which represents a significant distance concern; the 90-day break is notable and while the similar-going record shows two places from ten runs, the trip drop is the dominant factor to weigh.

runners_data.name: Tommy McJohn
runners_data.note: Adrian Paul Keatley's four-year-old has a 36-day break and a trainer who has been in good form (4 from 18 over 14 days); Mikey Sheehy rides and the horse's similar-going record of two places suggests enough ability to figure, particularly if the pace becomes competitive in Scenario B.

runners_data.name: Jkr Cobbler
runners_data.note: Jack Nicholls (5lb claim) partners this seven-year-old for Iain Jardine, who has sent out two winners from 33 runners over the past 14 days; a recent run 11 days ago and a similar-going record showing one place from seven qualifying runs gives a fair platform, and the horse handles this surface.

runners_data.name: Little Beck Annie
runners_data.note: Mark Winn rides this Peter Niven-trained four-year-old who won a 6f race on Good ground and wears a hood; she is on a quick turnaround at 11 days and her similar-going record is thin (no wins, no places from two runs), though the headgear and course-distance form are angles worth noting.

runners_data.name: Angel Of England
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves takes the ride for Alan Brown on this five-year-old who is flagged as fading in the finish and has been redistributed to the lead from a prominent role because no confirmed front-runner exists in the field; she controls the shape of this race entirely by default, not by design, and that distinction matters.

runners_data.name: Haworth Star
runners_data.note: Jack Garritty partners this six-year-old for Max Young, who carries a fade-in-finish flag and a similar-going record showing one win from eleven runs; the horse is a true hold-up type shown in midfield only because the map cannot accommodate all the rear-runners, and his best form on this surface (2nd, 6f, Standard) is the standout piece of similar-going evidence.

runners_data.name: Tickets
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen rides Ben Haslam's seven-year-old, who boasts the best similar-going record in the field — one win and three places from twelve runs — with a second and a third both coming over 6f on Standard ground at this course; though a true hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield position, his track record here is the strongest tactical argument for him thriving if he finds daylight.

runners_data.name: Ridgemaster
runners_data.note: Amie Waugh (3lb claim) partners her trainer Simon Waugh's four-year-old on the freshest turnaround in the field at just six days; the horse has placed on Good and Soft ground at 6-7 furlongs and his similar-going record shows one win and one place from five runs, making him one of the more interesting profiles if he can secure a handy position early.

runners_data.name: Vitalline
runners_data.note: Josephine Gordon partners Keiran Burke's eight-year-old who wears tongue-tie and blinkers and has an unbeaten similar-going exposure record — fifteen runs on Standard, including two wins and four places; the sheer volume of course-and-conditions experience is striking, and while a true hold-up horse redistributed to midfield, the proven Standard-surface record marks him as one to follow in the closing stages.

races.paceDynamic: Angel Of England is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this 14-runner 6f handicap on a Standard To Slow Newcastle AW surface, redistributed to the lead from a prominent style, meaning this race is likely to be run at a modest, uncontested tempo with no genuine rival willing to take her on early. The entire field is catalogued as hold-up types, but Haworth Star, Tickets, Ridgemaster, and others are genuinely prominent or mid-div horses who cannot all slot into their natural positions — Angel Of England and whichever of those pushes forward early will control the fractions without being pressured. A gentle, front-end gallop on a Standard To Slow surface over 6f is unlikely to produce a deep closing run from true hold-up horses, meaning the winners are likely to come from horses who travel handy or can reach striking position by the two-furlong pole. The race shape firmly favours hold-up horses who are actually prominent in style — those who can sit just off a soft pace and pounce inside the final two furlongs — rather than genuine back-of-the-field closers who will face too much ground to make up.

watchPoints.text: Tickets — if Andrew Mullen can slot him just off the pace rather than having to make up ground from the rear, his course-and-distance form on Standard gives him a material advantage over most of this field.

Ridgemaster — racing on a six-day turnaround with Amie Waugh's 3lb claim, his recent 6f placings on Good and Soft suggest he handles varying conditions, and if he pushes forward early he could outrun his redistribution and feature prominently.

Angel Of England — her tendency to fade in the finish is a significant flag when she is being relied upon as the sole pace-setter by default; watch whether Tom Eaves actually commits to the front or allows another horse to go on, which would reshape the entire pace map.

Vitalline — fifteen Standard-surface runs for Keiran Burke gives him an unmatched dataset on this exact track type; Josephine Gordon will need to find a clean passage from the rear, and any traffic in the final two furlongs could cost him a placing his form merits.

Miners Gamble — the drop from ten furlongs to six is extreme and bears monitoring in the early exchanges; if he travels kindly and is not asked to sprint, the fitness question from 90 days off is less critical, but his sectionals in the first two furlongs will tell a story about whether he can handle this trip.
